pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/34637

@rolfbjarne did you mean something like this?
pr_comments: No, to fix #34637 you need to pass `-Wl,-install_name,@executable_path/libfoo.dylib` to clang when compiling the dylib (or alternatively use `install_name_tool` after the dylib has been built).

As Rolf said this is not the correct way, we need to fix it on the cmake side. I tried a few things and couldn't get it to work, from reading cmake docs having https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/174f13637c1f5b422fa01f5cf8ff3911bca2f3e0/src/libraries/Native/Unix/CMakeLists.txt#L17 should actually be enough but for some reason it's not.

issue_context.title: Dynamic libraries in the microsoft.netcore.app.runtime.ios-x64 package has incorrect identity
issue_context.body:
Repro:

```shell
otool -l ~/.nuget/packages/microsoft.netcore.app.runtime.ios-x64/5.0.0-*/runtimes/ios-x64/native/*dylib | grep LC_ID_DYLIB -A 2
          cmd LC_ID_DYLIB
      cmdsize 184
         name /Users/runner/runners/2.165.2/work/1/s/artifacts/obj/native/netcoreapp5.0-iOS-Release-x64/System.IO.Compression.Native/libSystem.IO.Compression.Native.dylib (offset 24)
```

This should be something like `@executable_path/libSystem.IO.Compression.Native.dylib`.

CC @akoeplinger
comments:
<strike>Not sure what changed but at least on macOS I see the binaries now have identity like `@rpath/libSystem.IO.Compression.Native.dylib` which seems reasonable. Is this still relevant? Or just specific to iOS?</strike>

Nevermind, still broken in the iOS packages.

Tagging subscribers to this area: @safern, @viktorhofer
See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.

review_comments: Is `@executable_path` somehow recognized by the tool chain, e.g. the linker, and rewritten?  Or is that actually a directory special name recognized by iOS?

`@executable_path` is expanded to the directory of the main executable by the dynamic loader (dyld) on Apple platforms: https://www.mikeash.com/pyblog/friday-qa-2009-11-06-linking-and-install-names.html (when `@executable_path` is encountered when loading dynamic libraries).
